resolutions.covered_by: detached-scope-cannot-be-verified-by-a-decoy (new, invariant), with postcondition-scope-detached-by-its-own-action re-expected to the same ruling
resolutions.route: the guard, not the disclosure — the acceptance's second branch
resolutions.what_changed: `agent.check_state` no longer falls back to page-wide when the acted scope has detached. `live_scope()` is now `detached()`, read after each settle pass, and a detached scope returns None: the postcondition is UNVERIFIABLE, not page-wide and not false. Traced downstream before choosing it: None leaves `rec['postcondition_ok']` null, `verifier.STATE_CHANGING` ({click, press, go_back}) turns a null postcondition on a state-changing verb into a failed `actions_verified` check, `assemble_result` demotes the run to `failure:semantic` with reason `verifier FAIL: state-changing step(s) [N] carried no checkable postcondition`, and INV-2 drops the answer — loud and classified, not a silent pass. `url_contains` is exempt from the None (one address bar survives any frame), which keeps ADR-036 §1's third carve-out literally true. ADR-036 §4 is amended in place: the false sentence ('a detach is positive evidence the action did something ... a no-op detaches nothing') is struck with the strike-not-delete convention and the counter-example named, the §1 scope table's detach row now reads null/unverifiable, Consequences bullet 2 says plainly that ANY detach reopens §1's hazard in full when the fallback is page-wide, and specs/001-browser-contract.md and specs/decisions/INDEX.md carry the same ruling.
resolutions.watched_red: checks {"status": false, "trace_postconditions": false, "resolved_scopes": true, "reason_contains": false}, got {"status": "success", "answer": "NIMBUS-10K-2025", "reason": null} — the reviewer's fixture, committed as src/browser/fixtures/frames-decoy-detach.html, run against the page-wide fallback. Re-run with the expectations inverted to record what the tree actually produced: PASS on {status: success, verdict, trace_postconditions [true, true, null]} — a literal no-op click whose postcondition was earned by a decoy iframe, verdict PASS on every L1 check including `actions_verified`, answer delivered. Green after the guard: failure:semantic, trace_postconditions [true, null, null], 2.08s.
resolutions.expectation_changed: postcondition-scope-detached-by-its-own-action — R3's acceptance case — changes outcome: was {status: success, answer: NIMBUS-10K-2025, trace_postconditions [true, true, null]}, is now {status: failure:semantic, reason_contains 'carried no checkable postcondition', trace_postconditions [true, null, null]}, in 0.22s instead of 0.61s (and instead of the 2.55s settle burn R3 found). R3 is not reopened: R3 was a false NEGATIVE — a run asserting that an action which had worked did not — and the run now says it cannot tell, which is true. The case is kept, not deleted: it is the one case that measures the price of this ruling, and its provenance records the change and why.
resolutions.rejected_alternative: narrowing the fallback to the MAIN document instead of None was considered and rejected: it defeats this particular fixture (the decoy is an iframe) while leaving the identical laundering available with the decoy text in the host document, which is a one-line edit to the fixture. Only 'unverifiable' is sound without the successor-document identity T-M42-14 owns.
